title_en: Brain Cipher ransomware cripples Temporary National Data Center (PDNS 2)
kronologi_en: On 20 June 2024, PDNS 2 in Surabaya was encrypted by the Brain Cipher ransomware (a derivative variant of LockBit 3.0) after Windows Defender was disabled, paralyzing 282 services across 210+ central and regional agencies, including immigration autogates and education registration. The attackers demanded a USD 8 million ransom, which the government refused; on 3 July 2024 the group released the decryption key for free.
kualifikasi_en: Illegal access to and/or extortion of an electronic system (Article 30 in conjunction with Article 46 and Article 27B of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law), together with alleged negligence in fulfilling personal data protection obligations (UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law).
pelaku_en: The Brain Cipher group (a derivative variant of LockBit 3.0).
korban_en: The state and members of the public who use public services (airport immigration, education registration, licensing).
pse_en: The Temporary National Data Center (PDNS) 2 in Surabaya, under Kominfo, operated by Telkomsigma, with BSSN oversight.
objek_en: The availability and integrity of the Electronic System and the confidentiality of personal data.
akibat_en: Massive nationwide disruption of public services, the exposure of the absence of backups (backup/DRC), and a national data governance crisis.
nexus_en: The absence of data backups and Disaster Recovery mitigation — not the attack alone — was the fatal precondition that allowed a single encryption event to paralyze hundreds of agencies.

title_en: BKN civil-servant (ASN) data allegedly leaked and sold (~4.7M)
kronologi_en: On 10 August 2024, the BreachForums user 'TopiAx' claimed to have stolen 4,759,218 BKN records (NIP, NIK, name, place/date of birth, position, agency, address, contact, education) and offered them for ~USD 10,000. CISSReC verified a sample of 128 Aceh civil servants (ASN) as authentic; BKN stated it was investigating together with BSSN and Kominfo.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: ~4.7 million State Civil Apparatus (ASN) and ASN institutions.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of sensitive employment data of millions of state employees and added pressure to establish a data protection authority.
nexus_en: Weak access controls/encryption on the personnel database enabled exfiltration; the volume figure comes from the seller's claim, which was partially verified.

title_en: Elementary teacher arrested for intruding into BKN database (6.3 GB)
kronologi_en: In September 2024, police arrested a 25-year-old honorary elementary school teacher in Banyuwangi who had obtained BKN employee login credentials from BreachForums, downloaded ~6.3 GB of sample data, uploaded it to Pastebin, and then sold it for ~USD 8,000 on BreachForums and Telegram. The perpetrator was self-taught with no formal IT education.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
pelaku_en: An honorary elementary school teacher (initials BAG, 25) in Banyuwangi using BKN employee credentials from BreachForums.
korban_en: The civil servants (ASN) whose data was downloaded and traded.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Theft and sale of personnel data; the arrest and prosecution of the perpetrator.
nexus_en: The abuse of legitimate credentials (credential abuse) — rather than exploitation of a technical vulnerability — was the primary vector, indicating weak access management.

title_en: KPU voter roll (DPT) leak of ~204 million records ('Jimbo')
kronologi_en: Around 27-28 November 2023, 'Jimbo' offered 204,807,203 unique voter records from the voter roll (DPT) (NIK, family card number/KK, ID card/KTP, name, place/date of birth, marital status, address, polling station/TPS) for ~USD 74,000, with 500,000 sample records as proof. Resecurity later linked the compromise to info-stealer malware on KPU endpoints.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
scale_en: 204,807,203 unique voter records (252 million raw entries)
korban_en: Nearly all registered voters (the 2024 voter roll / DPT).
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of the PII of nearly all voters ahead of the February 2024 election and concerns over the integrity of the electoral database.
nexus_en: An info-stealer-infected operator endpoint served as the entry point; KPU did not officially confirm the origin of the data.

title_en: Bjorka leak of 1.3 billion SIM-card registration records
kronologi_en: On 31 August-1 September 2022, 'Bjorka' offered ~1.3 billion SIM registration records (NIK, phone number, operator, registration date; ~87 GB) for ~USD 50,000. Kominfo denied that the data originated from its systems; this incident opened the series of 'Bjorka' leaks in 2022.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: The majority of Indonesian mobile users (NIK-to-phone-number data).
pse_en: Disputed — the SIM registration data is associated with operators/Kominfo; Kominfo denied being the source.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of the NIK-to-phone-number linkage for most of the population; accelerated the passage of the UU PDP (Personal Data Protection Law).
nexus_en: The data controller was never confirmed; the government and operators denied responsibility against each other — marking an accountability vacuum.

title_en: Immigration Directorate passport data leak (~34.9 million)
kronologi_en: On 5 July 2023, researcher Teguh Aprianto reported that 'Bjorka' was selling data on ~34.9 million passport holders (name, passport number, validity period, place/date of birth, gender) covering the 2009-2020 period for ~USD 10,000. Immigration and BSSN investigated; authorities disputed whether the sample matched current data.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: ~34.9 million Indonesian passport holders.
pse_en: The Directorate General of Immigration (then under the Ministry of Law and Human Rights / Kemenkumham).
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of the passport PII of tens of millions of citizens; prompted calls to strengthen data protection oversight.
nexus_en: The root cause was not officially announced; Kominfo did not confirm a breach. The figure comes from the seller's claim, with the sample assessed as valid by researchers.

title_en: Bjorka sells ~6 million taxpayer IDs (NPWP), incl. President's
kronologi_en: On 18 September 2024, 'Bjorka' offered ~6 million NPWP (taxpayer ID) records (NIK, NPWP, name, address, contact, tax data) for ~USD 10,000; the sample named President Joko Widodo, Gibran, Kaesang, and two ministers. The Directorate General of Taxes (DJP) stated that its access logs showed no indication of a breach and opened an investigation.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
scale_en: ~6 million (reported up to 6.6 million) NPWP records
korban_en: ~6 million taxpayers, including senior state officials.
pse_en: The Directorate General of Taxes (DJP), Ministry of Finance.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of taxpayer PII including top officials; reignited debate over government cybersecurity.
nexus_en: DJP denied a system breach; the actual source was not confirmed. The figure comes from the seller's claim.

title_en: BAIS TNI military strategic-intelligence data allegedly breached
kronologi_en: Around 24-27 June 2024, 'MoonzHaxor' claimed to have breached BAIS TNI and posted sample files, offering the data for up to ~USD 7,000. The TNI Cyber Team stated it was investigating and temporarily took the BAIS server offline; officials described the material as old data.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: The TNI Strategic Intelligence Agency.
pse_en: The Strategic Intelligence Agency (BAIS) of the TNI.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Alleged exposure of military intelligence-related data; the server was taken offline for investigation.
nexus_en: Not fully confirmed by the TNI; the scale was not disclosed and the material was described as 'old data'.

title_en: INAFIS police fingerprint-identification system data leaked
kronologi_en: On 22 June 2024, 'MoonzHaxor' posted data from an alleged INAFIS breach (fingerprint images, emails, SpringBoot application files) for ~USD 1,000. The head of BSSN coordinated with Polri and stated that the data was old and that INAFIS services were running normally.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: The police fingerprint identification system (INAFIS).
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Alleged exposure of biometric data (fingerprints) related to the police identification system.
nexus_en: Not fully confirmed (described as 'old data'); the same perpetrator as the BAIS case, but with a different data controller.

title_en: President Jokowi's vaccine certificate exposed via PeduliLindungi feature
kronologi_en: In early September 2021, President Joko Widodo's vaccine certificate was accessed and circulated online after users exploited the vaccination-check feature in the PeduliLindungi app. The Health Minister stated that access to officials' data had been blocked and security improved; Kominfo argued that the NIK/vaccination data might have originated from other government sources.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged negligence in securing access to personal data on a public Electronic System (Article 35 and Article 36 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law).
scale_en: Individual exposure of a public figure (the President's vaccine certificate)
pelaku_en: Individuals who exploited the public app's certificate-check feature.
korban_en: President Joko Widodo; broader concern for PeduliLindungi users.
pse_en: The Ministry of Health (the PeduliLindungi operator at the time).
objek_en: The confidentiality of the health and identity data of a public figure.
akibat_en: Demonstrated that an app feature's vulnerability could expose sensitive data even of the head of state; access to officials' data was restricted.
nexus_en: Weak access control on a public feature (over-exposure by design), not mass exfiltration.

title_en: Health Ministry patient medical records leak (~6 million / 720 GB)
kronologi_en: On 6 January 2022, the Ministry of Health acknowledged that it was investigating an alleged leak of ~6 million patient medical records (~720 GB) being sold on RaidForums, including names, hospitals, patient photos, X-ray results, lab/COVID-19 results, BPJS referral letters, and radiology reports. The Ministry of Health coordinated with BSSN for the investigation.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: Patients from a number of hospitals.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of detailed clinical records (images and test results) from various hospitals; eroded public trust.
nexus_en: Centralization of data without adequate security; the volume comes from the seller's claim and was not independently confirmed.

title_en: BPJS Kesehatan national health insurance data leak (~279 million)
kronologi_en: In May 2021, the RaidForums account 'Kotz' sold data claimed to belong to ~279 million BPJS Kesehatan participants (NIK, ID card/KTP, phone, email, name, address, salary), with ~20 million accompanied by photos. The case was investigated by BSSN, the Cyber Crime Directorate (Dittipidsiber), and Kominfo; digital forensics were inconclusive in determining the source of the leak.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
scale_en: ~279 million records (claimed; largely duplicative relative to the population)
korban_en: BPJS Kesehatan (national health insurance / JKN) participants.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of the identity and health insurance data of most of the population; sharpened the data protection debate.
nexus_en: The source could not be forensically determined; the 279 million figure comes from the seller's/BPJS's claim, not an independent audit, and exceeds the actual number of participants (indicating duplication).

title_en: eHAC COVID-19 health-alert app exposes ~1.3 million users
kronologi_en: On 15 July 2021, the vpnMentor team discovered an unauthenticated eHAC Elasticsearch database that exposed ~1.3 million people (NIK, phone, photos, COVID-19 test results, travel/hospital data, staff credentials). After notification, the server was shut down on 24 August 2021; the Ministry of Health stated that the leak involved an old version of eHAC.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
pelaku_en: No confirmed malicious actor (an open Elasticsearch database, discovered by vpnMentor researchers).
korban_en: ~1.3 million users and travelers; data from 226 hospitals/clinics.
pse_en: The Ministry of Health (the old version of the eHAC app).
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of the sensitive health and travel data of more than a million people during the pandemic.
nexus_en: A database misconfiguration, not confirmed exfiltration; an old app that was not managed securely.

title_en: WannaCry ransomware hits Dharmais & Harapan Kita hospitals (Jakarta)
kronologi_en: In mid-May 2017, during the global WannaCry outbreak, Dharmais Hospital and Harapan Kita Hospital in Jakarta were hit by ransomware that encrypted Windows files via an SMB vulnerability. The director of Dharmais reported that nearly all computers were affected; medical records and billing systems were locked with a ransom of ~USD 300 in Bitcoin. Operations recovered via backups, and Kominfo stated that no medical records were leaked.
kualifikasi_en: Illegal access to and/or extortion of an electronic system (Article 30 in conjunction with Article 46 and Article 27B of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law), together with alleged negligence in fulfilling personal data protection obligations (UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law).
scale_en: Two major Jakarta hospitals; nearly all Dharmais computers affected
pelaku_en: The WannaCry ransomware (a global campaign; SMB exploitation).
korban_en: Dharmais Cancer Hospital and Harapan Kita Heart Hospital, Jakarta.
pse_en: Dharmais Hospital and Harapan Kita Hospital (affiliated with the Ministry of Health).
objek_en: The availability and integrity of the Electronic System and the confidentiality of personal data.
akibat_en: Temporary disruption of IT systems and access to medical records; recovery via backups with no confirmed data leak.
nexus_en: Systems were unpatched against the SMB vulnerability (EternalBlue); the existence of backups was the differentiator for recovery.

title_en: Legacy PeduliLindungi.id domain hijacked to show online gambling content
kronologi_en: Around 19-20 May 2025, the legacy PeduliLindungi.id site was found displaying online gambling promotion content after being compromised. Komdigi blocked the domain on 21 May 2025; health services had migrated to SatuSehat since 2023, and Telkom launched an internal investigation.
kualifikasi_en: Illegal access to and alteration/defacement of an electronic system (Article 30 and Article 32 in conjunction with Articles 46-48 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
scale_en: Compromise of a legacy app domain (no patient data leak)
korban_en: Visitors to the legacy PeduliLindungi.id domain.
pse_en: Telkom Indonesia (the domain manager after services migrated to SatuSehat).
objek_en: The integrity and authenticity of a public electronic system.
akibat_en: A reputational/security incident on a government health app domain; the site was blocked; no patient data was leaked.
nexus_en: An abandoned app domain (abandoned asset) that was not securely maintained became a hijacking target.

title_en: Alleged breach of SatuSehat instance for East Kotawaringin (Kotim)
kronologi_en: Around 7 August 2025, a new dark web forum user offered a database claimed to be from the SatuSehat instance for East Kotawaringin Regency (Kotim), containing timestamps, medical record numbers, BPJS numbers, names, gender, polyclinics, print status, and barcodes, with the data reportedly spanning 2020-2025.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
scale_en: A single regency-instance database (count not stated); data spanning 2020-2025
korban_en: Patients in East Kotawaringin Regency.
pse_en: The SatuSehat platform (Ministry of Health); the seller linked it to BPJS Kesehatan.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Alleged exposure of patient identities and health administrative data for a regency-level population.
nexus_en: A regional instance risks becoming the weak point of a national platform; the claim has not been confirmed by mainstream media or the Ministry of Health.

title_en: Ministry of Education (Kemendikbudristek) ~25 GB data leak claim
kronologi_en: In early February 2025, a BreachForums member (indexed via FalconFeeds.io) claimed to be selling ~25 GB of data attributed to Kemendikbudristek (name, identity number, gender, place/date of birth, phone, province/city ID). The ministry had not issued an official confirmation at the time of reporting.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: Participants/individuals in the Kemendikbudristek data.
pse_en: The Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Alleged exposure of personal data in the education sector; assessment of the claim's authenticity ongoing.
nexus_en: Not confirmed by the ministry; based on a single threat-intelligence-sourced report; the scale comes from the perpetrator's claim.

title_en: Attorney General's Office (Kejaksaan Agung) website defacement
kronologi_en: In February 2025, the official website of the Attorney General's Office (kejaksaan.go.id) was hit by a defacement attack, reported via social media around 10 February 2025. The perpetrator, via an Instagram handle, claimed to have accessed databases including employee, visitor, e-ticketing, and case data.
kualifikasi_en: Illegal access to and alteration/defacement of an electronic system (Article 30 and Article 32 in conjunction with Articles 46-48 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: The Attorney General's Office of the Republic of Indonesia (Kejaksaan Agung RI).
pse_en: The Attorney General's Office of the Republic of Indonesia.
objek_en: The integrity and authenticity of a public electronic system.
akibat_en: Defacement of a national judicial-sector website and claims of internal data access; reputational impact.
nexus_en: The defacement is confirmed; the claim of database control is the perpetrator's assertion, not officially confirmed.

title_en: UGM engineering faculty website defaced by 'Bangsin'
kronologi_en: In December 2022, a hacker using the alias 'Bangsin' defaced the 'FIND IT!' site of the UGM Faculty of Engineering (findit.ft.ugm.ac.id) with the message 'BANGSIN WAS HERE AGAIN' and an audio file. It was reported as a repeat incident by the same perpetrator; UGM's information security unit (DSSDI) handled it.
kualifikasi_en: Illegal access to and alteration/defacement of an electronic system (Article 30 and Article 32 in conjunction with Articles 46-48 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
scale_en: A single faculty web application (FIND IT! / findit.ft.ugm.ac.id)
korban_en: The Faculty of Engineering, Gadjah Mada University.
objek_en: The integrity and authenticity of a public electronic system.
akibat_en: Defacement of a university web application; no data theft was reported.
nexus_en: A recurring vulnerability in the faculty's web application; defacement only, without any data leak.

title_en: Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) ransomware attack and 1.5TB leak (LockBit)
kronologi_en: On 8 May 2023, BSI's ATM and branch services were paralyzed; LockBit claimed to have stolen 1.5 TB of data on ~15 million customers and employees. Negotiation logs showed the bank offered ~USD 10 million while LockBit demanded USD 20 million; after the talks failed, the data was published on 15-16 May 2023.
kualifikasi_en: Illegal access to and/or extortion of an electronic system (Article 30 in conjunction with Article 46 and Article 27B of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law), together with alleged negligence in fulfilling personal data protection obligations (UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law).
scale_en: ~15 million customers & employees; 1.5 TB of data
korban_en: ~15 million BSI customers and employees.
objek_en: The availability and integrity of the Electronic System and the confidentiality of personal data.
akibat_en: Multi-day service disruption and the leak of customer/employee data (contacts, financial documents, card data, passwords) on the dark web.
nexus_en: Layered defenses were penetrated; the ransom was not paid, so the exfiltrated data was published.

title_en: Bank Indonesia (central bank) Conti ransomware attack
kronologi_en: Bank Indonesia confirmed a ransomware attack that occurred in December 2021 and was reported by researchers in January 2022. Conti planted ransomware on more than a dozen systems and claimed ~13.88 GB of documents, which it began leaking. BI and BSSN stated that the attackers only obtained non-critical employee data and that public operations were not disrupted.
kualifikasi_en: Illegal access to and/or extortion of an electronic system (Article 30 in conjunction with Article 46 and Article 27B of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law), together with alleged negligence in fulfilling personal data protection obligations (UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law).
scale_en: ~13.88 GB of documents; non-critical employee data on more than a dozen systems
korban_en: Bank Indonesia (the central bank).
objek_en: The availability and integrity of the Electronic System and the confidentiality of personal data.
akibat_en: Compromise of internal employee documents and a partial leak; with no confirmed impact on public services according to BI.
nexus_en: Initial access to the internal network; mitigation limited the impact to non-critical systems.

title_en: Indodax cryptocurrency exchange hot-wallet hack (~$22M)
kronologi_en: On 11 September 2024, attackers drained the Indodax hot wallet of more than USD 22 million (including ~USD 14 million in ETH, USD 2.5 million in MATIC, USD 2.4 million in TRX, USD 1.4 million in BTC), as identified by SlowMist and CertiK. Indodax suspended the platform under the pretext of maintenance; Cyvers assessed that the tactics resembled Lazarus, but the attribution was not confirmed.
kualifikasi_en: Fraud and/or theft via an electronic system (Article 28 paragraph (1) of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law in conjunction with Articles 378/362 of the Criminal Code / KUHP) and alleged money laundering (UU 8/2010 / Anti-Money Laundering Law).
scale_en: More than USD 22 million in crypto assets
pelaku_en: Unknown (tactics assessed by researchers as resembling the Lazarus Group).
korban_en: Indodax and its users.
objek_en: The victims' assets and the integrity of the payment system.
akibat_en: Theft of >USD 22 million in crypto assets; temporary suspension of all services.
nexus_en: Compromise of keys/the hot wallet; the Lazarus attribution is a researchers' hypothesis.

title_en: KreditPlus customer data leak on RaidForums (~896k)
kronologi_en: Data on ~896,169 KreditPlus customers was sold on RaidForums, first by 'Megadimarus' (27 June 2020) and then by 'ShinyHunters' (16 July 2020), containing names, NIK, email, address, place/date of birth, phone, and employment and guarantor data. Kominfo and OJK requested clarification from the company.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: ~896 thousand KreditPlus customers.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure and sale of the identity-financial data of nearly 900 thousand customers; regulatory inquiry.
nexus_en: Illegal access to the customer database; the figure is ~896 thousand (not 'millions' as is sometimes stated).

title_en: Cermati fintech aggregator data breach (2.9 million users)
kronologi_en: Data on 2.9 million Cermati users was sold for ~USD 2,200 on a hacker forum, made public via Teguh Aprianto on 4 November 2020, containing names, email, address, phone, bank accounts, occupation, NPWP, and NIK. Cermati sent unauthorized-access warnings to users on 31 October and engaged BSSN and external experts.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
pelaku_en: Unknown (a seller on a hacker forum).
korban_en: 2.9 million Cermati users.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of highly sensitive identity and financial data of 2.9 million users; calls to reset passwords/enable 2FA.
nexus_en: Unauthorized access to the financial aggregator's database.

title_en: BRI Life insurance data leak (~2 million policyholders)
kronologi_en: In late July 2021, a RaidForums user offered ~460,000 documents from data on >2 million BRI Life policyholders for ~USD 7,000 along with a sample video, reportedly containing account details, ID card (KTP) copies, and tax data. Hudson Rock noted that several BRI/BRI Life employee computers were compromised, which could have facilitated initial access.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: >2 million BRI Life policyholders.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Alleged exposure/sale of policyholders' identity and financial documents; investigation with an independent team.
nexus_en: Employee endpoint compromise as a possible vector; the figure comes from the perpetrator's listing.

title_en: AdaKami pinjol abusive debt-collection case and OJK sanction
kronologi_en: In September 2023, a viral report alleged that a borrower had died as a result of intimidation by AdaKami debt collectors, along with allegations of fictitious orders used for harassment and excessive interest/fees. OJK summoned AdaKami (20-21 September 2023), ordered a thorough investigation and a complaints channel, and then imposed a warning-letter sanction for violations of debt-collection practices.
kualifikasi_en: Violation of consumer protection in the financial services sector and unlawful debt-collection practices (UU 4/2023 PPSK / Financial Sector Development and Strengthening Law & OJK Regulations / POJK on consumer protection); OJK administrative sanction.
scale_en: Unknown (individual borrower complaints; a viral alleged suicide)
pelaku_en: AdaKami's allegedly unlawful debt-collection practices (debt collectors).
korban_en: AdaKami consumers/borrowers.
objek_en: The rights, safety, and dignity of financial services consumers.
akibat_en: OJK administrative sanction; mandatory investigation; tighter oversight of online lending (pinjol) debt-collection practices.
nexus_en: Weak consumer protection governance and debt-collection practices; not a data leak.

title_en: Bank Jatim BI-Fast payment-system fraud (Rp119.9 billion)
kronologi_en: On 22 June 2024, between ~12:22 and 15:38 WIB, 483 anomalous BI-Fast transactions worth ~Rp119.96 billion drained Bank Jatim's funds. The perpetrators used accounts in other people's names to receive the transfers, then converted the proceeds into crypto. Four defendants were convicted of money laundering by the Surabaya District Court (PN Surabaya) on 6 August 2025 (two years each); the mastermind 'Deni' is at large.
kualifikasi_en: Fraud and/or theft via an electronic system (Article 28 paragraph (1) of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law in conjunction with Articles 378/362 of the Criminal Code / KUHP) and alleged money laundering (UU 8/2010 / Anti-Money Laundering Law).
pelaku_en: A money laundering syndicate (4 defendants convicted; the mastermind 'Deni' at large).
korban_en: Bank Jatim (the East Java Regional Development Bank / BPD).
pse_en: PT Bank Pembangunan Daerah Jawa Timur Tbk (Bank Jatim).
objek_en: The victims' assets and the integrity of the payment system.
akibat_en: Losses of ~Rp119.9 billion through exploitation of the BI-Fast fraud layer; criminal prosecution; part of a wave of BI-Fast attacks on regional banks.
nexus_en: A weakness in the participant's (bank's) fraud-detection layer, not the core BI-Fast system (per BI's statement).

title_en: Bank DKI / Bank Jakarta BI-Fast cyber breach (Rp227 billion)
kronologi_en: On 29 March 2025, Bank DKI's payment system was breached via BI-Fast, producing 807 anomalous transactions worth ~Rp227.1 billion against its current account at BNI. The monitoring team detected a sharp balance drop at ~11:00-11:20 WIB and activated the 'panic button' protocol at 11:44 WIB; PPATK froze the related accounts, with indications that the attacks dated back to 2024.
kualifikasi_en: Fraud and/or theft via an electronic system (Article 28 paragraph (1) of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law in conjunction with Articles 378/362 of the Criminal Code / KUHP) and alleged money laundering (UU 8/2010 / Anti-Money Laundering Law).
pelaku_en: A hacker syndicate (linked to the wave of BI-Fast attacks; investigation ongoing).
korban_en: Bank Jakarta (formerly Bank DKI).
pse_en: PT Bank Pembangunan Daerah DKI Jakarta (Bank DKI / Bank Jakarta).
objek_en: The victims' assets and the integrity of the payment system.
akibat_en: ~Rp227 billion in illegal fund flows via BI-Fast; account freezing by PPATK; triggered an OJK national inspection of regional banks' (BPD) cyber resilience.
nexus_en: Exploitation at the participant layer; part of the series of BI-Fast attacks on regional banks.

title_en: Tokopedia 91 million accounts breached and sold
kronologi_en: In March 2020, Tokopedia's user database was stolen. In early May 2020, a portion of ~15 million records was uploaded to a forum and the full 91 million database was sold on the dark web starting at ~USD 5,000, containing email, name, place/date of birth, mobile number, and hashed passwords; more than 200,000 credentials were later de-hashed and disseminated.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
pelaku_en: Sold by ShinyHunters on a forum/dark web; the initial actor was not named.
korban_en: 91 million Tokopedia users.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Mass exposure of 91 million users' data; cracked credentials circulated (risk of credential stuffing/phishing). Tokopedia urged password resets.
nexus_en: Illegal access to the database; accelerated momentum for the passage of the UU PDP (Personal Data Protection Law).

title_en: Bukalapak ~13 million accounts sold by Gnosticplayers
kronologi_en: In March 2019, Gnosticplayers sold a fourth batch on Dream Market; ~13 million of the 26 million records originated from Bukalapak (the breach dated to 2017). The data contained usernames, names, email, hashed passwords (salted bcrypt/SHA-512), and shopping history, offered for ~1.24 BTC (~USD 5,000).
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: ~13 million Bukalapak users.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of ~13 million credentials/personal details; the data was indexed by Have I Been Pwned (18 April 2019).
nexus_en: A 2017 data breach that was only sold in 2019; password hashing limited (but did not eliminate) the risk.

title_en: Bhinneka.com ~1.2 million accounts dumped online
kronologi_en: Bhinneka.com was breached on 27 January 2020; in July 2020 the database (~1.26 million records, two SQL files) was disseminated for free. The data contained IDs, names, email, gender, phone, salted hashed passwords, addresses, place/date of birth, social media IDs, and last login logs.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: ~1.26 million Bhinneka.com customers.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: ~1.26 million customer records made publicly available (risk of phishing/identity fraud); added to Have I Been Pwned.
nexus_en: Illegal access to the database; public exposure without monetization.

title_en: Lazada RedMart 1.1 million accounts breached (regional)
kronologi_en: On 29 October 2020, Lazada discovered illegal access to an old database of the RedMart grocery service. >1.1 million accounts were sold for ~USD 1,500 on a hacker forum, containing email, SHA-1 hashed passwords, names, phone, mailing/billing addresses, and some credit card numbers with expiry dates. Lazada stated that the data was more than 18 months old.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
pelaku_en: Unknown (a data broker on a hacker forum).
korban_en: 1.1 million RedMart customers.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: 1.1 million customer records exposed; a forced password reset and a report to Singapore's PDPC.
nexus_en: A legacy database that was not securely retired; the incident was centered in Singapore (RedMart), with the group operating across ASEAN including Indonesia.

title_en: IndiHome 26.7 million subscriber browsing-history leak
kronologi_en: In August 2022, 'Bjorka' posted a dataset of 26,730,798 IndiHome customer browsing histories (Aug 2018-Nov 2019) on BreachForums, covering dates, domains, platforms, browsers, URLs, plus NIK, email, phone, and gender. Kominfo summoned Telkom; Telkom/IndiHome did not confirm the leak.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: IndiHome customers.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of browsing histories alongside identity data (profiling, surveillance, targeted fraud); government investigation.
nexus_en: Unprotected storage of browsing histories linked to identities; Telkom denied it.

title_en: MyIndiHome 35 million customer records leaked
kronologi_en: In early July 2023, 'Bjorka' offered ~35.9 million MyIndiHome app records (~7 GB compressed), tagged 3 July 2023, claimed to contain email, phone, customer number, NIK, name, device type, address, and IP, for ~USD 5,000. Telkom Group stated that MyIndiHome data was secure and that it found no server attack.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: MyIndiHome app customers.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Alleged exposure of ~35 million customer identity records; Telkom was summoned by Kominfo and BSSN coordination.
nexus_en: Telkom denied it; the figure comes from the 'Bjorka' listing and CISSReC analysis.

title_en: PLN electricity customer data of 17 million listed for sale
kronologi_en: In August 2022, data on >17 million PLN customers was offered on a hacker forum (name, address, customer ID, meter number, kWh consumption). PLN stated that the data was a copy of a public dashboard, not from its direct transaction system; Kominfo and BSSN opened an investigation.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
pelaku_en: Unknown (the user 'loliyta'; linked to Bjorka, unconfirmed).
korban_en: >17 million PLN electricity customers.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of the names, addresses, and consumption data of 17 million+ households; added pressure for the PDP Bill (RUU PDP).
nexus_en: PLN denied a breach of its core system; the actor attribution is uncertain.

title_en: MyPertamina fuel-payment platform breach (44 million records)
kronologi_en: In November 2022, a dataset attributed to MyPertamina was leaked in CSV format, containing ~44 million records and ~6 million unique emails, plus names, place/date of birth, gender, address, phone, and purchase history. Have I Been Pwned indexed this breach (added in January 2024).
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: Users of the MyPertamina fuel-payment service.
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Exposure of the personal and transactional data of millions of fuel-payment users.
nexus_en: Illegal access/exfiltration; the 'Bjorka' attribution comes from a claim and was not independently confirmed.

title_en: Toll-road operator Jasa Marga (JMTO) breached by DESORDEN
kronologi_en: On 25 August 2022, DESORDEN announced that it had breached JMTO and exfiltrated ~252 GB from five servers. After Jasa Marga stated that no customer data was involved, DESORDEN reviewed and confirmed that the data was corporate and employee information. Jasa Marga shut down the affected servers and migrated its systems.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: PT Jasamarga Tollroad Operator (JMTO).
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Compromise of the corporate and employee data of the largest toll-road operator; affected servers were shut down.
nexus_en: Illegal access to corporate servers; the perpetrator confirmed that customer data was not affected.

title_en: PT KAI (Indonesian Railways) Stormous ransomware claim
kronologi_en: In January 2024, Stormous claimed to have breached PT KAI via VPN access using employee credentials and stolen employee, customer, tax, and corporate data, demanding ~11.69 BTC (~Rp7.7 billion) with a threat to publish in 15 days. KAI denied any evidence of a passenger data leak and stated that it was investigating.
kualifikasi_en: Illegal access to and/or extortion of an electronic system (Article 30 in conjunction with Article 46 and Article 27B of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law), together with alleged negligence in fulfilling personal data protection obligations (UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law).
scale_en: Unverified (claimed employee, customer, tax, and corporate data)
pelaku_en: The Stormous ransomware group (claimed access via VPN with employee credentials).
korban_en: PT Kereta Api Indonesia (KAI).
objek_en: The availability and integrity of the Electronic System and the confidentiality of personal data.
akibat_en: An extortion demand and threats to publish internal/customer data; KAI is investigating.
nexus_en: Claimed access via VPN credentials; the scope of the theft has not been verified (KAI denied it).

title_en: Lion Air Group (Malindo Air) passenger data of ~30 million leaked
kronologi_en: In September 2019, passenger data from the Lion Air Group subsidiary Malindo Air leaked to a forum, exposing passport details, addresses, and phone numbers (payment data was reportedly not affected). Kaspersky researchers found >30 million airline records on a forum, with a suspected misconfigured cloud server. Malindo confirmed it and notified Malaysian regulators while engaging AWS/GoQuo.
kualifikasi_en: Alleged failure of personal data protection (Article 35 and Article 57 of UU 27/2022 on PDP / Personal Data Protection Law) and illegal access to an electronic system (Article 30 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
korban_en: Passengers of Malindo Air / Thai Lion Air (Lion Air Group).
pse_en: Lion Air Group / Malindo Air (hosted via AWS and the GoQuo platform).
objek_en: The confidentiality and protection of data subjects' personal data.
akibat_en: Mass exposure of international passengers' PII including passport details; regulator notification and forensic investigation.
nexus_en: A misconfigured cloud server as the cause; cross-border (the group is headquartered in Indonesia, with a Malaysian subsidiary).

title_en: Deepfake videos of President Prabowo & ministers in nationwide 'aid' fraud
kronologi_en: Starting around December 2024, scammers spread AI deepfake videos featuring President Prabowo Subianto and other officials purportedly offering government aid. Victims were directed to WhatsApp numbers and asked for an 'administration fee' of Rp250,000-1,000,000 for fictitious aid. The National Police Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim Polri) arrested a 25-year-old perpetrator (JS) in Lampung on 4 February 2025; JS and AMA were handed over to prosecutors in April 2025.
kualifikasi_en: Creation/dissemination of AI-based manipulative content (deepfake) for fraud (Article 28 and Article 35 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law in conjunction with Article 378 of the Criminal Code / KUHP); manipulation of images/biometrics (UU 27/2022 / Personal Data Protection Law).
scale_en: ~100 victims across 20 of 38 provinces; ~Rp65 million (one cell)
pelaku_en: Suspects 'JS' (25, Lampung) and 'AMA' (arrested, on trial); said to be part of a wider syndicate.
korban_en: The general public; the impersonated figures: President Prabowo, Vice President Gibran, Finance Minister Sri Mulyani.
pse_en: Social media platforms (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, WhatsApp).
objek_en: The victims' assets, the honor of public figures, and the reliability of information.
akibat_en: ~100 victims across 20 provinces were defrauded of up to tens of millions of rupiah; two suspects were charged and put on trial.
nexus_en: The absence of any obligation to label/detect synthetic content and of guardrails worsened the spread of the deepfake fraud.

title_en: Undip student created AI deepfake pornography of schoolmates & teachers
kronologi_en: A Undip law student secretly photographed female students and teachers at SMAN 11 Semarang, then used AI deepfake/face-swap tools to create non-consensual pornographic images and a video titled 'Skandal Smanse' that was uploaded to X. The Central Java Regional Police (Polda Jateng) investigated; he was named a suspect and detained on 10-17 November 2025, with thousands of files found in his storage.
kualifikasi_en: Creation and distribution of AI-based non-consensual intimate content (Article 27 paragraph (1) and Article 35 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law; UU 44/2008 on Pornography; UU 12/2022 on Sexual Violence Crimes / TPKS, Article 14) and violation of biometric personal data (UU 27/2022 / Personal Data Protection Law).
scale_en: ~30 victims (including minors aged 16-19); thousands of files found
pelaku_en: Chiko Radityatama Agung Putra, a law student at Diponegoro University (Undip), Semarang.
korban_en: Female students, alumnae, and teachers of SMA Negeri 11 Semarang.
objek_en: The honor, dignity, sexual integrity, and personal data (facial images) of the victims.
akibat_en: ~30 victims identified (some minors); the suspect was detained and charged under the Pornography Law, the UU ITE, and the Criminal Code (KUHP), facing 9-12 years.
nexus_en: The accessibility of generative AI tools without safeguards enabled the mass production of non-consensual intimate images.

title_en: AI deepfake 'resurrecting' Suharto used to urge votes for Golkar
kronologi_en: On 6 January 2024, Erwin Aksa uploaded to X an AI deepfake reconstructing the face and an imitated voice of the late Suharto (who died in 2008), in which the synthetic 'Suharto' urged people to vote for and support Golkar. The clip spread widely ahead of the 14 February 2024 presidential election.
kualifikasi_en: Dissemination of AI-based false/manipulative information capable of causing unrest or harming honor (Article 28 paragraph (3) and Article 27A of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
scale_en: Viral on X ahead of the 14 Feb 2024 election
pelaku_en: The Golkar Party; uploaded by deputy chairman Erwin Aksa.
korban_en: Indonesian voters (a synthetic likeness of the late former President Suharto).
objek_en: Public information order, the integrity of the democratic process, and the honor of a public figure.
akibat_en: Widely criticized as a manipulative electoral deepfake of a deceased authoritarian figure; became an international reference point; no legal action taken.
nexus_en: The absence of rules on political deepfakes/labeling allowed synthetic content of a deceased figure to circulate in a campaign.

title_en: Deepfake videos of presidential candidates before the 2024 election
kronologi_en: Ahead of the 14 February 2024 election, unlabeled AI deepfake videos showing presidential candidates Prabowo and Anies purportedly speaking fluent Arabic circulated on TikTok. Reporting noted that deepfakes of all three presidential tickets also spread, with the potential to mislead voters.
kualifikasi_en: Dissemination of AI-based false/manipulative information capable of causing unrest or harming honor (Article 28 paragraph (3) and Article 27A of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
scale_en: Circulated on TikTok ahead of the 14 Feb 2024 election; affecting several candidates
korban_en: Presidential candidates Prabowo Subianto and Anies Baswedan (and the other ticket).
objek_en: Public information order, the integrity of the democratic process, and the honor of public figures.
akibat_en: Disinformation targeting voters during a national election; flagged by researchers and fact-checkers; some content was removed by the platform.
nexus_en: A pattern (not a single incident) marking the electoral information space's vulnerability to synthetic content.

title_en: Deepfake of Finance Minister Sri Mulyani fabricating a remark
kronologi_en: In mid-August 2025, a deepfake manipulated an authentic recording of a speech by Finance Minister Sri Mulyani (7 August 2025 at an ITB forum) so that she appeared to call teachers a 'burden on the state'. The Ministry of Finance's communications bureau (Deni Surjantoro) confirmed the clip was an AI deepfake made from incomplete fragments; the official Indonesia.go.id account also debunked it.
kualifikasi_en: Dissemination of AI-based false/manipulative information capable of causing unrest or harming honor (Article 28 paragraph (3) and Article 27A of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law).
scale_en: Circulated widely on social media for several days, mid-August 2025
korban_en: Finance Minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati / the Ministry of Finance.
pse_en: Social media (the specific platform was not named).
objek_en: Public information order, the integrity of the democratic process, and the honor of a public figure.
akibat_en: A reputational attack on a senior minister during a politically tense period; warned to have the potential to cause unrest; potential prosecution under the UU ITE/criminal law.
nexus_en: The ease of manipulating a public recording into a deepfake; the absence of detection/labeling worsened its spread.

title_en: OJK-documented wave of AI voice-cloning & deepfake financial fraud
kronologi_en: OJK reported that the two most common AI fraud methods in Indonesia are voice cloning (imitating the voice of a relative/colleague/official to request an urgent transfer) and deepfake video, including bypassing biometric liveness/eKYC checks. Losses reached Rp7.8 trillion between November 2024 and November 2025, with 70,000+ AI-enabled fraud reports as of August 2025.
kualifikasi_en: AI-based synthetic identity fraud / voice cloning and circumvention of authentication (Article 28 and Article 35 of the UU ITE / Electronic Information and Transactions Law in conjunction with Article 378 of the Criminal Code / KUHP).
scale_en: Rp7.8 trillion (~USD 474 million) in losses Nov 2024-Nov 2025; 70,000+ reports as of Aug 2025
korban_en: Bank/fintech customers and the general public.
pse_en: Banks and fintech platforms (eKYC providers); OJK (the regulator).
objek_en: The victims' assets and the reliability of authentication (eKYC/voice biometrics).
akibat_en: Hundreds of millions of US dollars in consumer losses; OJK and Komdigi issued AI governance guidance and strengthened biometric protocols.
nexus_en: A pattern/aggregate marking the maturation of voice cloning and synthetic eKYC abuse, together with regulatory gaps.
